title: Kroketter av ägg (Egg Croquettes)
description: Prepared with cream, gelatin, and white pepper.
steps: Cook eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, shell and cut into fine dice.
Fry butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes.
Carefully stir in the diced eggs together with the rinsed gelatin dissolved in 1 tablespoon hot water.
Season the stew with spices and treat as in recipe no. 49.
Form the croquettes into round shapes.
Serve as a breakfast dish with stewed peas or spinach.

title: Kronans kaka (Crown Cake)
description: A cake made with potato, sweet almonds, and rusks.

ingredients.name: washed butter for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon washed butter for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons crushed rusks for the pan

steps: Wash the butter and beat it with the sugar, egg yolks, and grated potato for half an hour.
Blanch the almonds, grind or pass them through an almond mill, and stir in along with the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the batter into a buttered and rusk-sprinkled pan and bake in fairly weak oven heat.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it stand 10-15 minutes before turning it out.
Serve it poured over with lemon cream.

title: Kronärtskocksbottnar à la Princesse (Artichoke Bottoms à la Princesse)
description: Prepared with artichoke, asparagus, and peas.
steps: Place the bottoms in the water with the butter added; when it boils again, remove them with a slotted spoon and let them drain.

title: Kroppkakor (Potato and Meat Dumplings)
description: Prepared with potatoes, wheat flour, and smoked ham.
steps: Peel and cook the potatoes, drain the water, and mash with a fork or press through a ricer and let cool.
Add the salt, egg and most of the flour (save some flour for rolling out).
Work the dough very little on the board and form into round cakes.
Peel the onion; cut the ham and onion into cubes and fry and season.
Make a hole in the middle of each cake and fill with a teaspoon of the fried ham mixture, then press the hole well closed.
Place the dumplings in boiling salted water and let simmer slowly until they float up, or approximately 10 minutes.
Serve with clarified butter.

title: Kroppkakor (Potato and Meat Dumplings)
description: Prepared with potatoes, egg yolks, and smoked ham.
steps: Rinse and brush the potatoes clean, peel raw and boil until just tender.
Drain the water well, and let the potatoes stand for about 10 minutes with the lid slightly ajar so the steam escapes, then press through a potato ricer and let cool.
Whisk the egg and egg yolks and add together with 2 hg of the flour and salt.
Work the dough slightly on a pastry board with the remaining flour and roll into a long roll, which is cut into pieces; these are then rolled like rusks.
Fry the pork and ham together with the onion if desired, and add the spices.
Make a depression in each dumpling, which is filled with pork pieces, then press the dumpling closed well.
Put the dumplings in boiling salted water and let simmer gently with the lid on for about 10 minutes.
Test with a whisk to see if they are done.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve warm with melted butter.
It is best to test-cook one dumpling before the others are finished, to determine if the dough is of proper firmness.

title: Krusbärsgelé (Gooseberry Jelly)
description: Prepared with gooseberries, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: sugar equal in weight to the juice
ingredients.sourceText: sugar equal in weight to the juice

steps: Clean the berries, rinse them and cook them very slowly with the water until they begin to burst apart.
Pour them into cheesecloth and let them drip until the following day.
Weigh the juice and dissolve the sugar in the cold juice.
Then let it come to a boil and boil rapidly for 15-20 minutes under careful skimming.
The jelly is ready when a drop of it, poured onto a plate, quickly sets.

title: Krusbärskompott (Gooseberry Compote)
description: A gooseberry compote made with sugar and water.

ingredients.name: 1 lit. halvmogna, gröna, tunnskaliga krusbär (omkr. 5 hg.)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 lit. halvmogna, gröna, tunnskaliga krusbär (omkr. 5 hg.)

steps: Make a clear, syrupy syrup from the sugar and water.
Top and rinse the gooseberries well and drain on cloth.
Place them in the sugar syrup and cook until they begin to crack, but do not cook until they fall apart.
Remove the gooseberries with a slotted spoon and place in a compote bowl.
Cook the syrup until it is syrupy and pour it immediately over the berries.
Serve cold with whipped cream.

title: Krusbärskräm (Gooseberry Cream)
description: Prepared with gooseberries, flour or potato starch, and water.

ingredients.name: 8 dcl. fresh or 6 dcl. preserved gooseberries
ingredients.sourceText: 8 dcl. fresh or 6 dcl. preserved gooseberries

ingredients.name: mondamin flour (23 gr.) or 1 1/2 tbsp. potato starch (23 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 tbsp. mondamin flour (23 gr.) or 1 1/2 tbsp. potato starch (23 gr.)

steps: Top and tail the gooseberries, rinse them and let them drain.
Cook a thin, clear syrup from the sugar and water.
Add the gooseberries and let them cook until they begin to burst.
Mix the flour with 2 tbsp. cold water or French wine and use to thicken the cream.
Let the cream cook for 5 minutes if thickened with mondamin, but only 2 minutes if thickened with potato starch.
Taste the cream and add more sugar if needed.
Stir occasionally until cold, then pour into a compote dish.
Serve with cream or milk.

title: Krustader av vatten (Water Crisps)
description: Prepared with water, egg yolks, and oil or lard.

ingredients.name: cooking oil or 3/4 kg lard for frying
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 litre cooking oil or 3/4 kg lard for frying

steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, add water, egg yolk and seasonings while whisking with a steel whisk.
When the batter is even and smooth, pour in the cooking oil.

The pan in which the crisps are to be cooked should be deep but not wider than a teacup. At the same time as the oil is poured into the pan, place the iron mold in it to heat; otherwise the batter will not stick to the iron.

Pour the batter into as many spoonfuls as there are forms on the iron. When the oil is hot, dip the iron into the batter, but not all the way to the edge, and hold it first for a minute over the heat so that the crisps set slightly, otherwise they will be blistery.
Hold the iron thereafter in the hot oil until the crisps have turned golden brown, loosen them with a larding needle and lay them upside down on gray paper to drain.
Fill them immediately with warm stew and serve as a side dish or as garnish for fish and meat dishes.
The crisps can be stored 2-3 weeks if placed in a tin with a tightly closed lid, but must then be heated in the oven before the filling is added.
Crisps can be filled with stewed poultry and mushrooms, calf sweetbreads and truffles, asparagus, crayfish, lobster, shrimp and fish, oysters, and with vegetables and purées.

The crusts can be stored 2—3 weeks if placed in a tin with a tightly sealed lid, but must then be heated in the oven before the filling is added.
Crusts can be filled with stew of poultry and mushrooms, calf's sweetbreads and truffle, asparagus, crayfish, lobster, shrimp and fish, oysters as well as with vegetables and purées.

title: Krustader med stuvning av kalvbräss och tryffel (Crisps with Stewed Calf Sweetbreads and Truffles)
description: Prepared with calf sweetbreads, truffles, and sweetbread.
steps: The calf sweetbreads should soak in water for 1 hour so that the blood is drawn out.

Blanch them (place in cold, lightly salted water and let them cook in it for 10 minutes) and then place in 1/2 litre of boiling water with salt, to cook about 1/2 hour or until they become white and firm.
Lay them on a sieve so the stock drains well. Cut the sweetbreads into fine cubes and sauté in the butter until it becomes clear.
Squeeze it out of the butter with a spoon. Then sauté the flour with the butter for 2 minutes, add the sweetbread stock and cream, and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes.
Add the calf sweetbreads and the finely cut truffle, and let the stew come to a boil and taste it.
Lastly stir in the whisked egg yolk, let the stew simmer and fill the crisps immediately.
Serve as a side dish.

title: Kryddlimpor (Spiced Loaves)
description: Prepared with rye, wheat flour, and skimmed milk.

ingredients.name: finely chopped bitter orange peel
ingredients.sourceText: 3 tbsp finely chopped bitter orange peel

steps: From the rye flour, a portion of the wheat flour, the lukewarm milk, and the yeast mixed with salt, make a dough as described on page 462, and let the dough rise to double its size.
Warm the syrup somewhat in a pot together with the fat and spices and work into the dough along with enough wheat flour that the dough becomes quite firm.
Let the dough rise again, then work it well with the rest of the wheat flour on the work surface and divide into 6-8 parts.
Work each part until it is smooth and without cracks, and then roll it into an oblong roll, which is placed on warm, soft baker's cloth, on which is placed a baking cloth that is floured.
Place the rolls next to each other with the baking cloth drawn up in a large fold between each roll and cover.

When the rolls are risen, tip them onto a bread peel, place on buttered, lukewarm baking sheets, prick along the length with a landing needle, brush with cold milk and bake in not too hot an oven for about 1/2 hour.
When the rolls are light, take them out, brush with hot water and place between cloths so that the crust becomes soft.
The dough can be mixed with cold liquid the evening before it is to be baked.

sourceSteps: Make a dough from the rye flour, some of the wheat flour, the lukewarm milk, and the yeast mixed with salt, as described on page 462, and let the dough rise to double its size.
Warm the syrup slightly in a pot together with the fat and spices and work into the dough along with enough wheat flour to make the dough quite stiff.
Let the dough rise again, then work it well with the rest of the wheat flour on the baking board and divide into 6-8 parts.
Work each part until it is smooth and without cracks, then roll it into an oblong roll, which is placed on a warm, soft baking cloth with a baking cloth laid on it which is floured.
Place the rolls next to each other with the baking cloth drawn up in a large fold between each roll and cover.

When the rolls are risen, turn them out onto a bread peel, place on greased, lukewarm baking sheets, nick along the length with a skewer, brush with cold milk and bake in a not too hot oven for about 1/2 hour.
When the rolls are light, remove them, brush with hot water and place between cloths so the crust becomes soft.
The dough can be mixed with cold liquid the evening before it is to be baked.

title: Kryddskorpor (Spiced Rusks)
description: Prepared with cream, rye, and wheat flour.
steps: Melt the cream in the milk — the rusks become thereby softer. — The dough is made as described on p. 462 and 1 dcl. syrup is added at once. When the dough has risen to double its size, it is worked again with the rest of the syrup, the orange peel, the fennel, the beaten eggs, the melted butter and the rest of the flour except 1 hg. of the wheat flour, which is saved for baking. The dough is turned out onto a floured work surface, kneaded and divided into 12 parts, which are worked well, rolled out into long, thin buns, which are laid on buttered pans, allowed to rise and baked in a warm oven. When the buns are cold, they are cut into 1 1/2 cm. thick slices, which are split into upper and lower rusks, cut, if desired, and dried as wheat rusks (see no. 957).

title: Kräftsmör (Crayfish Butter)
description: Prepared with crayfish, butter, and water.

ingredients.name: butter, equal weight to the crayfish shells
ingredients.sourceText: butter, equal weight to the crayfish shells

steps: Boil the crayfish as in no. 171. Clean them; tails, claws and all fat are used for stews or sauces, the remainder is weighed and an equal weight of butter is taken.
Pound the shells and butter in a stone mortar into a fine mass, which is allowed to melt in a water bath with stirring and strain through fine cheesecloth into a bowl with cold water.
When the butter is half set, form it into balls, which should weigh 10 gr. each.
Store them well covered in brine and use for sauces and stews.

Alternatively, all fat from the crayfish together with the shells can be pounded with the butter into a fine mass, which is passed through a hair sieve and pressed through muslin. This butter has an exquisite fine taste but should be used within 1-2 days, as it becomes rancid quickly.
Lobster butter is prepared from lobster shells in the same way.

Butter can be colored green with spinach coloring or with pistachios. The pistachios, 120 gr., are blanched, ground through an almond mill, pounded in a stone mortar with 30 gr. butter and passed through a hair sieve.

title: Kräftsoppa (Crayfish Soup)
description: A soup made with crayfish, fish or meat or broth, and water.

ingredients.name: 2 to 2 1/2 liters fish or meat broth
ingredients.sourceText: 2 to 2 1/2 liters fish or meat broth

steps: Place the crayfish in boiling salted water and cook for 15-20 minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and let drain.
Remove the tails and claws, and pound the shells with the butter.
Place the shells in a pot together with the bread, add the boiling broth (preferably fish broth), and let the soup simmer slowly over low heat for about 1 hour.
Strain the soup, add the crayfish tails and serve very hot.
If the soup needs to be colored, it should be done with crayfish butter and not with cochineal.

title: Kräftsoppa (Crayfish Soup)
description: A soup made with crayfish, fish stock or stock, and madeira or sherry.

ingredients.name: 3 dozen large or 4 dozen small crayfish
ingredients.sourceText: 3 dozen large or 4 dozen small crayfish

ingredients.name: fish stock or clear stock
ingredients.sourceText: 3.5 liters fish stock or clear stock

steps: Rinse the crayfish, place them in the water with salt added, and let them cook 10–15 minutes, depending on size, and should preferably cool in the cooking liquid.
Remove the meat from the tails, remove the intestine and cut the tails in half lengthwise, then serve them in the finished soup.

Remove the stomach from the shells and pound these very finely in a mortar together with the butter, then place the mixture in a pot and let it fry over the heat while stirring for 10 minutes, then add the cold stock.

Let the soup cook slowly with a lid for about half an hour. Pass it through a sieve and let it stand for a quarter hour so that the crayfish butter has time to float to the surface. Skim off the butter and fry it with the flour for 2 minutes, add the stock little by little, and let the soup cook for 5 minutes, then season it with the spices and wine.

Whisk the egg yolks and cream in the soup bowl and pour the soup in while whisking. Add the crayfish tails along with the asparagus tips, which have been warmed in a water bath, and serve the soup very hot.

title: Kräftsoufflé (Crayfish Soufflé)
description: Prepared with crayfish, white pepper, and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: 1 score crayfish or 2 hg crayfish tails
ingredients.sourceText: 1 score crayfish or 2 hg crayfish tails

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp butter (10 gr) for the mold

steps: Rinse the crayfish and place in {{source-10}} with 40 gr coarse salt and 2 dill stems, boil for 10 minutes.
If using salted crayfish tails, soak them in milk for several hours.
Clean the crayfish, cut the tails and claws into pieces and scrape out the fat thoroughly.
Fry the butter and flour together for 2 minutes.
Add the milk while stirring and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes.
Pour into a bowl; when cooled, add the egg yolks one at a time and stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Mix in the crayfish meat and fat along with the seasonings and the egg whites beaten until stiff peaks form.
Taste and adjust seasonings.
Pour into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined mold and bake in regular oven heat for about 45 minutes.
If the soufflé becomes too brown on top, cover with buttered paper.
Serve immediately upon removal from the oven as a middle course with crayfish sauce or stirred butter.
If using a metal form, bake in a water bath in the oven for about 1 hour and turn out.

title: Kurrysoppa (Curry Soup)
description: A soup made with celery, carrot, and beef stock.
steps: Prepare the celery root and carrot in the usual way, cut into fine strips and cook soft in the beef stock, which is then strained.
Place the roots in the soup bowl.
Brown the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the strained stock and let it boil under stirring for 5 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks and whisk them into the soup, which is then seasoned with curry powder, salt and cayenne pepper and poured over the vegetables in the soup bowl.
Rinse the rice grains, place them in boiling salted water and let them cook until soft, about 15 minutes.
Drain them in a colander, rinse with cold water and let them stand in the oven for a few minutes, stirring with a fork until they are dry and warm.
Arrange on a platter and serve with the soup.

title: Kuvertbröd (Rose Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and poppy seeds.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl. Distribute the butter in flakes in the flour and work it in with the fingertips, then stir in the milk and the yeast, dissolved with the salt and sugar and the finely crushed cardamom, if desired.
Work the dough very well and roll out into 15 round buns, in which a cross is made with a sharp knife.
Place the breads on buttered baking sheets, allow to rise for approximately 1 1/2 hours, brush with whipped egg or milk, sprinkle with poppy seeds and bake in a warm oven for 20-25 minutes.
The breads can be formed as horns and treated as above.
The dough can also be rolled out into 30 thin sticks, which are cut diagonally, allowed to rise, brushed with milk, sprinkled with salt and baked until beautifully brown in a warm oven.
Instead of yeast, 2 teaspoons baking powder can be used, but the breads are then baked immediately they are rolled out.

title: Kyckling à la Tua (Chicken à la Tua)
description: Prepared with chickens, lard, and rice.

ingredients.name: clear veal or chicken broth
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter clear veal or chicken broth

steps: Pluck the chickens, singe them, draw them (see p. 299 f.), rinse very well and dry, then remove the breastbone carefully.
Rinse the rice, blanch it in hot water, add it to the boiling broth and let it cook until almost tender, then remove and let it cool.
Cut the goose liver and truffle into small cubes and mix into the rice together with the wine and seasonings.
Stuff the chickens with the rice, sew them shut, truss them (see p. 300) and cover with the lard, which is tied on with fine twine.
Place them in a pot, no wider than they just fit, add the boiling broth, bring to a boil, skim, and then keep at a temperature of 90°.
At this temperature let the birds lie until they are tender, or about 1 hour.

Halve them, place on a warm platter, cover with the sauce and garnish with the artichoke bottoms, warmed in a water bath, on each one 1 slice of truffle and on top of the truffle 1 mushroom cap, sautéed in butter, as well as salad lettuce and parsley.
For the sauce, brown the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add 4 dcl. of the broth in which the birds cooked, and let the sauce cook 5 minutes.
Whip the cream with the egg yolks and add it; then let the sauce simmer and season with the lemon juice and seasonings.
Finally add the cold butter.

title: Kycklingar, stekta i ugn (Chickens Roasted in the Oven)
description: Prepared with chickens, broth, and butter.
steps: Clean the chickens, singe them (see page 299), cut them open down the back, draw them, rinse very well and dry.
Brown the butter in a long pan, add the chickens with breasts down and brown on top of the stove, while basting frequently with the butter in the pan.
Turn them, sprinkle with salt, thin with the hot broth and let them roast in the oven until tender, or 15-20 minutes. During this time baste them frequently.
Cut the chickens in half, arrange, garnish and serve as in the preceding recipe.
Serve the sauce as a gravy by straining it, skimming it, boiling it together and seasoning it, or else thicken it and add cream (see no. 429).

title: Kärnmjölkspudding (Buttermilk Pudding)
description: A pudding made with buttermilk, gelatin, and lemon.
steps: Flavor the buttermilk with sugar and with grated zest and juice of lemon.
Rinse the gelatin in cold water and dissolve it in a little hot water, then stir it into the milk.
If the milk is so cold that the gelatin does not mix properly with it and the milk appears streaked, place it briefly under whisking over heat until it has an even color.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed mold and set it out to stiffen.
Turn it out and serve.

title: Kåldolmar (Cabbage Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with cabbage, rice, and beef.
steps: Carefully loosen the cabbage leaves from the stem, place them in boiling salted water and blanch for about 5 minutes.
Remove them with a slotted spoon and let them drain on a cloth, then cut off the coarsest part of the main vein.
Rinse the rice grains, scald in hot water, pour into a colander and let them drain.
Melt the butter in a pot, pour in the milk, let it come to a boil, add the grains and let them cook with stirring until they are almost soft, then set aside to cool.
Prepare the ground meat as in recipe no. 637.
Mix the ground meat and the cold grains well and season carefully. (If the meat is too hard, thin it with a little more cream.)
Place one tbsp. of the meat mixture on each cabbage leaf, roll it up and tie with fine twine that has been dipped in boiling water.
Brown the butter in a frying pot, add the rolls and brown nicely, thin with a little of the boiling broth and let them cook slowly with the lid tightly closed for about 2 hours.
During this time, add more broth as needed.
Remove them, cut off the twine and place the rolls on a platter.
Strain the sauce, skim off fat and pour it over them.
The rice grains can be omitted, but then calculate more meat.

title: Kåldolmar (Cabbage Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with cabbage, rice, and beef.
steps: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage head and carefully loosen the remaining leaves from the core so they remain whole.
Lay them in boiling water to blanch for a few minutes, then lay them on a cloth to drain.
Rinse the rice grains in cold water and scald them in boiling water; add 3 cups milk and let the grains cook until soft.
When done, pour them out to cool.
Treat the meat and bacon as in the preparation of meat forcemeat.
Mix the egg, 1 cup milk, the spices and the cooled grains together.
Cut away the thickest part of the main vein from the cabbage leaves.
Place one tablespoon of forcemeat on each cabbage leaf, roll it up and tie it with fine twine previously dipped in hot water.
Brown the rolls in butter, add the bouillon and let them simmer slowly with the lid on for at least 1 hour, shaking them occasionally.
Remove them, take off the twine, skim the sauce, add the cream and bring to a boil while whisking.
Place the cabbage rolls on a carrot and pour the sauce over them.

title: Kåldolmar (Cabbage Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with cabbage, rice, and beef.
steps: Carefully loosen the cabbage leaves from the core, place them in boiling salted water and blanch for about 5 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a cloth, then trim away the thickest part of the central vein.
Rinse the rice, scald it in hot water, drain in a colander and let it cool.
Melt the butter in a pot, add the milk, bring to a boil, add the rice and cook while stirring until it is almost tender, then set aside to cool.
Prepare the meat forcemeat as in recipe no. 637.
Mix the forcemeat and the cooled rice well and season carefully. (If the forcemeat is too firm, thin it with a little more cream.)
Place one tbsp. of the mixture on each cabbage leaf, roll it up and tie with fine twine previously dipped in boiling water.
Brown the butter in a braising pot, add the rolls and brown them nicely, thin with a little of the boiling broth and simmer slowly with the lid tightly closed for about 2 hours.
During cooking, add more broth as needed.
Remove them, cut off the twine and place the rolls on a carrot.
Strain the sauce, clarify it and pour it over them.
The rice grains can be omitted, but then more forcemeat should be calculated.

title: Kålrotspuré (Rutabaga Purée)
description: Prepared with broth, white pepper, and cream.
steps: Wash, peel and cut the rutabaga into cubes. Fry butter and flour together, and dilute with 1 liter of the broth. Add the roots and let them cook until soft, after which they are passed through a sieve.
Pour the passed mass back into the soup pot and add the remaining broth. Bring the purée to a good boil, skim and season.
Whip the cream in the soup bowl, and pour in the soup with vigorous whisking.

title: Körsbärskräm (Cherry Cream)
description: Prepared with cherries, potato starch, and water.

ingredients.name: mondamin (45 gr.) or 3 tbsp. potato starch (45 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 tbsp. mondamin (45 gr.) or 3 tbsp. potato starch (45 gr.)

steps: Clean the cherries, rinse them and let them drain.
Crush half of the berries in a stone mortar.
Put both the whole berries and the crushed berries into the cold water together with the sugar and let them cook until the berries are soft.
Strain through a colander.
Pour the juice back into the saucepan, taste it and thicken with the flour mixed with 1 dcl. cold water.
Let the cream cook while stirring for 5 minutes.
Pour into a compote dish rinsed with lukewarm water, sprinkle with sugar to prevent a skin from forming, let cool and serve with cream or milk.

title: Körsbärssaft (Cherry Juice)
description: Prepared with cherries and sugar.
steps: Clean the cherries but do not remove the pits, rinse and let them drain.
Layer them alternately with the sugar in a stone crock.
Place a plate on top and seal it with a dough made from coarse rye flour and water so that it becomes completely airtight.
Place the crock in a water bath and let it cook for 6 hours, counted from the moment the water boils.
Strain the juice immediately and bottle it warm or cold, cork the bottles and seal with resin.
The berries can be dried and advantageously used for soups.

When it has cooled, pour it over the berries and seal the bottles well again.

title: Körsbärssalad (Cherry Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with cherry, cherries, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: sugar per kilogram of berries
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 kilogram sugar per kilogram of berries

steps: Rinse the berries, pit them, weigh them and let them soak in the vinegar for 24 hours, then drain the vinegar.
Layer the cherries with granulated sugar, spices and pits in a jar, and pour enough of the vinegar over so that it covers the berries.
Bind the jar and let it stand in a cool place.
After 6 days, strain the liquid, cook it until it is syrupy, let it cool and pour it back over the berries.
Repeat this once more if the liquid seems thin.

title: Körsbärssoppa (Cherry Soup)
description: A soup made with cherries, lemon, and potato flour.

ingredients.name: fresh cherries or 5 deciliters dried cherries
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter fresh cherries or 5 deciliters dried cherries

steps: Rinse the cherries in a colander and let them drain; pound half of them in a stone mortar until the stones are crushed.
Put the crushed cherries in 1 1/2 liters of water with the lemon zest and let them cook 3/4 hour.
Strain the berries out, add sugar to the liquid, bring it to a boil, and thicken with the potato flour mixed in 1/2 coffee spoon cold water, then let the soup cook 2 minutes.
Remove the stones from the remaining cherries, cook the berries in the rest of the water with {{source-6}}, and add them to the finished soup.
Serve preferably cold with whipped cream and rusks or biscuits.
If using dried cherries, rinse them in lukewarm water, pound them so the stones are crushed, and let them soak a few hours in the water in which they will be cooked.

title: Kött och Rötter (Meat and Roots)
description: Prepared with chuck or brisket, water, and salt.
steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water and cut into oblong pieces of suitable size for serving.
Boil the water with the salt, add the meat and skim when it boils.
Add the pepper.
Let the meat cook slowly with the lid on until tender, approximately 2 1/2 hours, adding boiling water as needed.
Peel the rutabaga, cut into even cubes, and place on top of the meat 1/2 hour before it is done.
In a sauce pan, fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, pour in the meat cooking liquid and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes, then taste and adjust seasoning.
Transfer the meat and vegetables to a warm serving dish and pour the sauce over.
The butter may be omitted; in that case, stir the flour in a little cold water and add it to the stew, which should then boil for 8 minutes.

title: Köttbullar (Meatballs)
description: Prepared with beef, veal, and fat.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, cut it together with the fat into cubes and pass it three times through a meat grinder.
Whip up the eggs and milk, add the crushed rusks and let them soak.
Peel the onion, chop it finely and fry it in 1/2 tablespoon of the butter.
Mix the soaked rusks and spices into the forcemeat.
Work the forcemeat until it becomes cohesive like a dough.
Finally add the fried onion.
Brown the butter in a frying pan, shape the meatballs with spoons dipped in lukewarm water, and brown them in the hot butter.
Add 1 cup of boiling water, cover with the lid, and let the meatballs cook through for 1.5 hours.

title: Köttbullar (Meatballs)
description: Prepared with beef, veal or pork, and fat.

ingredients.name: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the onion (optional)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the onion (optional)

steps: If desired, beef alone may be used.
Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, remove sinews and membranes, cut into cubes, mix with the fat and spices and run 6 times through a meat grinder.
Mix the meat mixture with the whipped egg, egg yolk and breadcrumbs and work for 1 hour, during which the cream is added by the tablespoon.
If desired, add at the end the finely chopped onion, fried in the butter.
Test the mixture to see if it is sufficiently seasoned and of the right consistency by frying a small ball of it.
Heat a frying pan slowly and brown the butter in it.
Form the mixture with two wooden spoons, dipped in lukewarm water, into small balls, which are browned nicely in the butter and placed in a pot.
Whisk out the frying pan with the broth and pour the sauce over the meatballs, which then fry with a tight lid for 10-15 minutes.
Arrange on a warm serving plate, whisk up the sauce, taste and adjust seasoning, and pour over the balls.
The sauce can also be prepared as in recipe no. 429.

steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, cut together with the bacon into cubes and pass three times through a meat grinder.
Pound it in a stone mortar until it becomes fine and smooth.
Whisk the eggs and milk, add the crushed rusks and let them soak.
Peel the onion, chop it finely and braise it in {{source-7}}.

Place the forcemeat in the oven, brown it and then thin it with a little boiling stock or water, baste around every tenth minute and let it fry for about 1 hour.

title: Köttgrotta (Meat Cake)
description: A cake made with beef, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung in hot water, remove sinews and membranes, cut into dice and run 7-8 times through the meat grinder.
Scrape the lard and cut into fine dice.

Blend the forcemeat with the spices and lard and work vigorously for 1/2 hour, then add the rusks, beaten egg, egg yolk and flour and work the forcemeat another 1/2 hour; meanwhile add the cream tablespoon by tablespoon.
Test the forcemeat (see Forcemeat, page 316) to check if it is sufficiently seasoned and of proper firmness.
Shape the forcemeat into 2 oblong round balls, which are cooked in the hot pork fat until they take on a nice brown color.
Transfer the forcemeats to boiling broth and simmer with the lid closed for 1 hour.
Remove them, cut into slices, garnish with parsley and serve with vegetables.
Leftovers of meat cake are cut into thin slices and served on the smorgasbord.

Test the forcemeat to see if it is sufficiently seasoned and has proper consistency.
Shape into 2 oblong round balls, which are cooked in the hot pork jelly until they have taken on a nice brown color.
Transfer the forcemeat balls to the boiling broth and let them cook with a closed lid for 1 hour.
Remove, cut into slices, garnish with parsley and serve with vegetables.
Leftover meat grotta is cut into thin slices and served at the sandwich table.

title: Köttjärpe (Meat Loaf)
description: Prepared with pork, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, remove sinews and membranes, and cut into cubes.
Scrape the lard and cut likewise into cubes.
Grind the meat and lard 6 times through a meat grinder, the last time together with the potatoes.
Work the forcemeat for 1 hour together with the seasonings, the beaten egg and egg yolk, and the milk, adding the latter by the spoonful so the forcemeat does not separate.

Grease a long pan with butter, add the forcemeat in the form of an oblong ball, smooth it with a spoon dipped in lukewarm water.

title: Köttkorv (Meat Sausage)
description: Prepared with beef, pork, and lard.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in cold water.
Cut it into pieces, remove sinews and membranes, and pass the meat 3 times through the meat grinder.
Then beat it well.
Cut the lard into fine cubes.
Pass the potato (which should not be too thoroughly cooked) through the grinder.
Boil the milk and let it cool.
Work all the ingredients well together for 1 hour and then stuff into well-cleaned curved casings, not too tightly.
Rinse the sausages with cold water and rub them in with a mixture of salt, sugar, and potassium nitrate.
The meat sausage can then either be laid down in saltwater or smoked for 2 days. In the latter case, a smaller amount of milk is used for thinning and it is stuffed somewhat tighter.

title: Köttkroketter (Meat Croquettes)
description: Prepared with meat, broth, and rusks.

ingredients.name: fried or boiled meat cut into cubes
ingredients.sourceText: 5 cups fried or boiled meat cut into cubes

steps: Melt butter and flour together, thin with broth, add the meat, and let the stew cook 10 minutes, then season.
Spread the mixture on a flat plate to cool, and form small sugar-top-shaped croquettes.
Roll them in crushed rusks, dip in whipped egg and roll again in crushed rusks, then let them dry for 1/2 hour.
Heat the lard, cook the croquettes golden brown in it and place on gray paper to drain.
Garnish with parsley and serve with mushroom or brown sauce, or together with stewed vegetables.

title: Köttpudding med blomkål (Meat Pudding with Cauliflower)
description: A pudding made with meat, cauliflower, and cooking liquid.

ingredients.name: Meat mixture as in recipe no. 632
ingredients.sourceText: Meat mixture as in recipe no. 632

ingredients.name: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the mold

steps: Prepare the meat mixture as in recipe no. 632.
Trim the cauliflower and soak it in vinegar-mixed water for 1 hour.
Place it in boiling water with salt and cook until tender but not falling apart.
Divide the cauliflower head into pieces and save the cooking liquid.
Fry the butter and flour together for 2 minutes, gradually add the cooking liquid, and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, season the braised vegetables with spices and let cool.
Grease a pudding mold with cold butter and dust with breadcrumbs.
Layer the meat mixture and the braised vegetables alternately in the mold; the first and last layer should be meat.
Cook the pudding in a water bath in the oven or on the stovetop for 1 1/2-2 hours.
Unmold, garnish with a ring of cooked cauliflower and serve with gravy (recipe no. 429) or with clarified butter.
Brussels sprouts may be used instead of cauliflower.
The pudding can also be baked in an ovenproof mold in the oven and is then ready in about 1 hour.

ingredients.name: For the mold: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 g.)
ingredients.sourceText: For the mold: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 g.)

steps: Scrape and chop the meat finely.
Sauté the butter with the onion and flour 2 minutes, add the boiling milk and let the sauce simmer while stirring 5 minutes; remove from heat and stir until cooled.
Then add the egg yolks, one at a time, and stir the mass 10 minutes, then mix in the meat and season the stew with spices.
Last, fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks, and pour the mass into a buttered and breadcrumb-coated pudding mold with a lid and let it simmer in a water bath on the stove for about 2 hours.
Turn out, garnish with slices of pickled cucumber or tomatoes and parsley.
Serve with brown gravy sauce (see p. 218) or with reduced sauce (see no. 429), mixed with finely chopped pickled onion, pickles or pickled cucumber.

title: Köttsky (Meat Stock)
description: Prepared with beef, veal or lamb or pork or chicken or game, and bones.

ingredients.name: cheap cuts of beef such as neck and legs
ingredients.sourceText: cheap cuts of beef such as neck and legs

ingredients.name: raw or roasted remnants of veal, lamb, pork, chicken and game
ingredients.sourceText: raw or roasted remnants of veal, lamb, pork, chicken and game

ingredients.name: bones and sinews, all well chopped
ingredients.sourceText: bones and sinews, all well chopped

ingredients.name: 2 carrots, cleaned and cut into slices
ingredients.sourceText: 2 carrots, cleaned and cut into slices

ingredients.name: 1 celery, cleaned and cut into slices
ingredients.sourceText: 1 celery, cleaned and cut into slices

ingredients.name: meat broth or water to cover the meat
ingredients.sourceText: meat broth or water to cover the meat

steps: In an iron pot, brown a generous amount of butter or lard
Add the meat and bones and brown them well together with the onions, carrots, celery, and white peppercorns
Pour in enough meat broth or water so that it is level with the meat
Skim well and simmer slowly for 5-6 hours
Strain the stock through a fine sieve or cloth and boil down further if desired
Let it stand until the following day so that the fat solidifies
When the stock is to be used, remove the solidified fat cake
If not all stock is used at once, the remainder should be boiled up with the fat, which may solidify again
If the fat cake lies undisturbed over the stock, it can be kept several weeks without spoiling

title: Köttsoppa (Meat Soup)
description: A soup made with marrow or brisket, carrots, and parsnip.

ingredients.name: marrow pipe, brisket, or neck
ingredients.sourceText: 2 kg marrow pipe, brisket, or neck

steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in cold water
Chop it into two pieces and place it in cold water
Bring quickly to a boil, skim well, and salt
Let the soup cook slowly with a tight-fitting lid for 3–4 hours
After about 2 hours, add the sautéed vegetables
When the soup is done, cut the vegetables into pieces and serve them in the soup bowl
Finally, add the chopped parsley, bring the broth to a boil, and pour it into the soup bowl
The meat can either be served in the soup cut into pieces, or separately with horseradish sauce

title: Köttsoppa (Meat Soup)
description: A soup made with beef or marrow, parsnip, and carrots.

ingredients.name: beef rib or marrow bone
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 kg beef rib or marrow bone

steps: Dry the meat with a cloth, wrung out in cold water, and chop into four pieces.
Place it in cold water, bring quickly to a boil and skim well.
Add the salt and the prepared vegetables and let the soup cook with a tightly closed lid for 3-4 hours or until the meat is very tender.
When the vegetables and leek are soft, remove them, cut with a vegetable knife into nice pieces and place in the soup bowl.
Strain the soup and skim off the fat well.
Return it to the pot, add the parsley, let the soup come to a boil, season with salt and pepper and pour into the soup bowl.
Serve the meat separately with horseradish sauce or also in the soup, cut into small pieces.

title: Köttstuvning i snäckor (Meat Stew in Shells)
description: Prepared with meat, veal, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Leftovers of roast or poultry (approximately 250 gr. meat)
ingredients.sourceText: Leftovers of roast or poultry (approximately 250 gr. meat)

ingredients.name: butter (20 gr.) for the shells
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tbsp. butter (20 gr.) for the shells

ingredients.name: flour for the egg mixture
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tsp. flour for the egg mixture

ingredients.name: 2 dcl. milk for the egg mixture
ingredients.sourceText: 2 dcl. milk for the egg mixture

ingredients.name: 1 can of mushrooms for garnish (1/4 litre)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 can of mushrooms for garnish (1/4 litre)

steps: Cut the meat into fine cubes.
Let the veal sweetbread soak in water, changing the water until all blood is drawn out.
Blanch it for 10 minutes, rinse with cold water and let drain in a sieve.
Carefully remove cartilage and membranes and cut the sweetbread into small cubes.
Cut the mushrooms likewise into cubes and save the broth.
Fry the sweetbread and mushroom pieces in the butter until clear, then remove with a spoon.
Fry the flour with the butter for 2 minutes, add the various liquids and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the meat, mushrooms and sweetbread and season the stew with spices.
Grease six to eight shell dishes with butter and place the meat stew in them.
For the egg mixture, beat the eggs well with the flour, milk and spices.
Heat a griddle and grease it with butter.
Make small omelets from the egg mixture and place one on each shell.

title: Lammbringa med Kurry och Ris (Lamb Breast with Curry and Rice)
description: Prepared with lamb, rice, and sauce.

ingredients.name: For the sauce: 1 teaspoon grated red onion
ingredients.sourceText: For the sauce: 1 teaspoon grated red onion

ingredients.name: For the rice: 2 deciliters rice grains (2 hg)
ingredients.sourceText: For the rice: 2 deciliters rice grains (2 hg)

steps: Treat and cook the breast as in the previous recipe. Cut it into pieces, which are covered to keep them warm. Strain the broth and skim it well.

For the sauce, sauté the onion in the butter, add the flour and sauté it with the butter and onion for 2 minutes, add the broth a little at a time, and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes, then season it with curry powder (about 1 teaspoon), stirred with 1 tablespoon warm water, and the sugar.

Rinse the rice grains in cold water, scald in hot water, place in boiling, salted water and let them cook until soft — 15-20 minutes — then strain them through a colander, immediately rinse with cold water, place in a warm oven and stir often with a fork, until they are separated and all water has evaporated.
Arrange the rice in a ring on a round serving platter and sprinkle with a little dry curry. Arrange the meat in the center of the platter and pour the sauce over. Garnish with parsley.

title: Lammkotletter med maitre d'hôtel-smör (Lamb Chops with Maître d'Hôtel Butter)
description: Prepared with lamb chops, butter, and white pepper.
steps: Lamb chops should be cut with long bones and be approximately 2 cm thick.
Dry them with a cloth wrung out in hot water, trim, pound on both sides and rub in with the spice mixture.
Fry them in the browned butter 6-8 minutes on each side, arrange in a circle on a round serving dish, and slip paper frills on the bones.

On each chop place a small slice of maître d'hôtel butter, which is prepared as follows: rinse the parsley, wrap it in a cloth, clean it, chop it finely and wring it hard in a cloth, after which it is mixed well with the butter, lemon juice and pepper.
Form the butter in a damp cloth into a roll of finger thickness and let it lie in the cloth, which is placed on ice or in a cold place, until it is hard.
Serve the chops with French or fried potatoes as a breakfast dish.

On each cutlet place a small slice of maitre d'hôtel butter, which is prepared as follows: rinse the parsley, wrap it in a cloth, clean it, chop it finely and wring it hard in a cloth, after which blend it well with the butter, lemon juice and pepper. Shape the butter in a damp cloth into a roll of a finger's thickness and let it lie in the cloth, which is placed on ice or in a cold place, until it is hard. The cutlets are served with French or fried potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Lammkotletter à la Maintenon (Lamb Chops à la Maintenon)
description: Prepared with lamb chops, white pepper, and veal or chicken.

ingredients.name: 1/2 hg (approximately 50 g) cooked veal or chicken

steps: Lamb chops should be cut with long bones and be approximately 2 cm thick.
Dry them with a cloth wrung out in hot water, trim, pound on both sides and rub in with the spice mixture.
Cut the meat, tongue and truffle into small, even dice.
Fry the butter and onion with the flour for 2 minutes, add the stock and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beaten egg yolk together with the meat and mushroom, season the stuffing with the spices and parsley and let it cool.
Fry the chops 4 minutes on one side in half of the butter.
Lay them on a cutting board with the fried side up.
Divide the stuffing into 6 equal parts and spread it out on the fried side of the chop and brush with the beaten egg yolk.
Fry the remaining butter in the frying pan, place the chops in with the stuffing side up and gratinee in the oven for approximately 8 minutes.
Place on a hot serving dish, whisk the pan with the meat jus, let the sauce come to a boil, season with 1 teaspoon cold butter and pour over the chops.
Slip paper frills on the bones.
Garnish with peas or French potatoes and parsley and serve as a breakfast or side dish.

title: Lammkotletter à la Nelson (Lamb Chops à la Nelson)
description: Prepared with lamb chops, white pepper, and rice.
steps: Treat and season the chops as in recipe 538, lightly fry them in the butter and place on a plate.
Rinse the rice grains and let them drain well.
Sauté them together with the onion in the butter until it is clear, then add the broth and let the grains simmer with stirring until they are soft — add more broth if needed.
Pass the grains through a sieve, blend with the egg yolks and a little thick cream and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Pipe the rice mixture beautifully through a piping bag onto the top of the chops, sprinkle with the grated cheese and pour the melted butter over it.

Place the chops in a long pan and gratinée in a warm oven for 8-10 minutes, place on a hot plate with parchment paper, garnish with parsley and serve with brown sauce (see recipe 430) and dwarf potatoes.
The chops will be juicier if they are braised over charcoal.

title: Lammnoasetter (Lamb Noisettes)
description: Prepared with lamb, white pepper, and lard.

ingredients.name: small potatoes cooked in stock
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 liter small potatoes cooked in stock

steps: Dry the fillets with a cloth wrung out in hot water and cut into 12 slices, which are lightly flattened.
Rub with seasonings, roll up and wrap in thinly cut lard slices.
Brown in butter, add boiling bouillon and braise covered until tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the lard slices and arrange the noisettes in a circle on a round serving dish.
Place a small round goose liver slice on each noisette.
Place the asparagus, reheated in a water bath, in the center of the dish.
Arrange the small potatoes around.
Garnish the arrangement with parsley and serve with truffle sauce (see recipe 433).

title: Lammstek (Lamb Roast)
description: Prepared with lamb, lard, and white pepper.
steps: The roast, which should have hung so it is tender, is dried, pounded, larded, and the shank bone is cut off.
It is larded most on the outer thigh and back, the knuckle is broken to facilitate carving, then the roast is rubbed with a mixture of salt and pepper.

A roasting pan is heated, the butter is browned in it along with some of the lard, the roast is placed in it with the inner thigh up and browned for about 1/2 hour in a warm oven, during which it is frequently basted with the fat in the pan.
It is diluted with the boiling broth or water and allowed to roast until tender, or about 1 1/2-2 hours; during which it is basted every 10 minutes.
Place on a warm serving platter and carve at the table. Serve with white beans and vegetables or vegetable patties, and the strained, skimmed meat gravy or with thickened sauce.

title: Landshöfdingsoppa (County Governor's Soup)
description: A soup made with barley, apples, and juice.
steps: Rinse the groats and put them on in cold water.
Rinse the apples, cut them into wedges, remove the cores, and add them when the groats come to a boil.
When the groats are soft and the apples are broken down, pass the soup through a sieve.
Return the soup to the pot, add the sugar and lemon juice, and give it a boil.
Whip the egg yolks and cream together in the soup bowl and mix in the soup with vigorous whisking.
Serve with gooseberry preserve and biscuits.

title: Laxpudding (Salmon Pudding)
description: A pudding made with skim milk, potatoes, and cream.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter (10 gr.) for the mold

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons crushed rusks for the mold

steps: Rinse the salmon, cut it into slices and let it soak in the skim milk for about 3 hours, take it out and wrap it in a cloth or white paper.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices and arrange them alternately with the salmon in a buttered and breadcrumb-lined pudding mold.
Beat the eggs with the flour, pour the milk mixture and the egg mixture into the mold.
Sprinkle the pudding with parsley and bake in the oven for about 40 minutes.
Serve with melted butter or currant sauce.

title: Laxpudding med risgryn (Salmon Pudding with Rice Grains)
description: A pudding made with rice, skimmed milk, and white pepper.
steps: Treat the salmon as in the preceding recipe and cut it into dice.
Rinse the rice grains, scald them in hot water, add to the boiling milk and let them cook, stirring, until almost soft; thin with a little more milk if needed.
Pour out and add the cold butter at once; when the grains have cooled, fold in the beaten egg yolks, the diced salmon and the seasonings.
Last fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Taste the mixture carefully, pour it into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined pudding mold, sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of the breadcrumbs and bake in ordinary oven heat for about 1 hour.
Serve with clarified butter.

description: Prepared with liver, pork, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the liver and let it soak in water for 1/4 hour.
Pat it dry and remove the membranes.
Slice the liver and turn the slices in a mixture of flour, salt and white pepper.

Arrange on a platter, place the pork slices around it, and pour the sauce over.

title: Leverkorv (Liver Sausage)
description: Prepared with liver, pork, and lard.
steps: Cut the liver into pieces and let it soak in cold water overnight.
Pour off the water and pour boiling water over the liver a couple of times.
Boil the pork meat and lard and let them cool.
Cut the pork meat into pieces and pass through the meat grinder.
Also grind the liver and pass it through a sieve.
Cut the lard into cubes and mix with the rest of the forcemeat.
Chop the lard and melt it in a pan.
Fry the chopped onion in it.
Strain off the liquid and mix it into the forcemeat along with all the spices and pork broth.
The mixture, which should be fairly loose, is filled into straight pork casings.
Prick the sausages carefully with a needle and cook slowly for ½ hour.

title: Lingondricka (Lingonberry Drink)
description: Prepared with lingonberries, tartaric acid, and water.
steps: Clean the berries, crush them with a wooden pestle and place in a crock.
Dissolve the tartaric acid in the hot water and add together with the cold water.
Stir the mixture well, cover it and let it stand for 2 days, stirring occasionally.
Strain the berries in cheesecloth and let them drain naturally as long as any juice drips from the cloth, or approximately 1 1/2 days.
Add the sugar to the juice, which is then stirred slowly for 1 hour.
Treat the juice as in the previous recipe. Dilute with water to taste when serving.
The remaining pulp can be made into a simpler juice by adding 1 1/2 liters water, 15 grams citric acid and 6 hectograms sugar, which is used first.

title: Lingonpäron (Lingonberry Pears)
description: Whole peeled pears cook slowly in a cinnamon-scented syrup made from strained lingonberry juice and sugar. The pears are kept with the reduced berry syrup poured over them.
steps: Clean the lingonberries, rinse them and cook with the water until they fall apart.
Pour them into a cheesecloth to drip.
Peel the pears, cut a cross into each pear, scrape the stems and cut them down to half length.
After peeling, place them in fresh water.
Cook the lingonberry juice with the sugar and cinnamon to a thick syrup.
Place the pears in and allow to cook very slowly until they are soft and clear.
Place them in a crock or jar.
If the syrup is not sufficiently thick, cook it down and pour it over the pears.

title: Lingonsylt (Lingonberry Jam)
description: A fruit preserve made with lingonberries, water, and sugar.
steps: Clean the lingonberries, preferably rinse with warm water and let drain well.
Cook the sugar and water approximately 15 minutes while skimming frequently, thereafter pour in the berries and let the jam simmer slowly while skimming until the berries appear clear.
If the lingonberries cook too long, the jam becomes dark.
Pour the jam into warm, dry jars and let cool.
Bind the jars with parchment paper (see page 505).
For simpler lingonberry jam, the sugar can be reduced or replaced with syrup.

title: Linskotletter (Lentil Cutlets)
description: Prepared with lentils, onion, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Clean and rinse the lentils, place them in soft, cold water and cook until mushy.
Peel the onion, cut it into cubes and brown it in the butter.
Pass the lentil mash twice through a meat grinder together with the crushed breadcrumbs and onion.
Cook the corn flakes for a few minutes in 1/2 liter of water; when cooled, stir them into the lentil mash together with the beaten eggs.
Season the mass and form into small cutlets, which are fried until nicely brown in the butter.
Serve with stewed pálstemackor or fried potatoes as a breakfast or dinner dish.

title: Linssoppa (Lentil Soup)
description: A soup made with lentils, smoked ham, and onion.
steps: Rinse the lentils and soak them the day before.
Scrape the ham and cut into pieces, scrape the celery, peel the onion and blanch it, then chop everything fairly finely.
Fry in 1 tablespoon of butter together with the lentils.
When the butter is absorbed, add the broth and let the soup slowly cook with a tightly closed lid.
When the lentils are soft, strain the soup.
Fry the remaining butter with the flour and add the lentil purée.
Let the soup cook for 10 minutes and taste and adjust seasoning.
Whisk the egg yolks and cream in a soup bowl and add the soup with vigorous whisking.
Scrape celery and cook in salted water, cut into slices, bread and fry in butter.
Cook the ham and cut into strips.
Serve the celery and ham in the soup. If desired, frankfurter sausage can be served in the soup instead.
